title: Descent of rational representations generated by a kernel-fixed vector
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $q:H\to G$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] with scheme-theoretic kernel $K$. Faithfully flat means that tensoring with $F[H]$ over $F[G]$ is exact and detects zero modules. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational $H$-module: an $F$-vector space with a coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[H]$ satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities. Let $0\ne v\in V$ be fixed by $K$, meaning that its restricted coaction is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$, equivalently $kv=v$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Let $W$ be the smallest $H$-subcomodule of $V$ containing $v$ (the intersection of such subspaces). Then $W$ is finite-dimensional, $v\ne0$ in $W$, $K$ acts trivially on all of $W$, and its $H$-action descends uniquely to a rational $G$-action. Thus the pullback of the descended coaction along $q^*:F[G]\to F[H]$ is precisely the original coaction on $W$. The kernel need not be reduced or central.

source.place: Lemma 5.15 (normal-subgroup invariants are a rational submodule) and Theorem 5.13 (quotient universal property), printed pp.101--102; apply 5.13 to H -> GL(W). Smallest subcomodules exist by intersections; the finite-dimensional hypothesis is already on V.

proof.text: Linear-algebra preparation. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free] choose bases of the kernel and image of any $F$-linear map $d:M\to N$, and of $M/\ker d$ and $N/\operatorname{im}d$. Lift quotient bases to obtain decompositions $M=\ker d\oplus L$ and $N=\operatorname{im}d\oplus L'$, with $d|_L$ an isomorphism onto its image: uniqueness of finite basis expansions [def-weil-pbc-free-module] constructs its inverse. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] tensors both these direct-sum decompositions and this inverse. Consequently $\ker(d\otimes1_R)=(\ker d)\otimes_F R$ for every $F$-algebra $R$, and every injective $F$-linear map stays injective after tensoring. These conclusions also hold with an arbitrary $F$-vector space in place of $R$. If $U,U'\subseteq M$, apply this kernel assertion to $M\to(M/U)\oplus(M/U')$ to get $(U\otimes_F R)\cap(U'\otimes_F R)=(U\cap U')\otimes_F R$ inside $M\otimes_F R$.

source.place: Proposition 4.31, printed p.96, basis-coefficient argument; explicit split-linear-map preliminaries over the field.

proof.text: The family of $H$-subcomodules of $V$ containing $v$ is nonempty, since it contains $V$. For two members $U,U'$, their coaction sends $U\cap U'$ into $(U\otimes_F F[H])\cap(U'\otimes_F F[H])=(U\cap U')\otimes_F F[H]$ by step 1. Thus their intersection is again a member, with the coaction identities inherited by the injective tensor inclusions. Choose a member $W_0$ of minimal dimension. Each $W_0\cap U$ contains $v$ and has dimension at most that of $W_0$, hence by minimality has the same dimension and equals $W_0$. Thus $W_0$ is contained in every member and is their intersection $W$. It is finite-dimensional as a subspace of the finite-dimensional $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], and $v\ne0$ in $W$ because its inclusion into $V$ is injective.

source.place: Lemma 5.15, printed p.102, applied to the generated submodule; the finite-dimensional minimal-intersection construction is written out.

proof.text: Put $C=F[K]$, and let $\rho_K:V\to V\otimes_F C$ be the restricted coaction. Define $d(x)=\rho_K(x)-x\otimes1$ and $I=\ker d$. Step 1 identifies $I\otimes_F R$ with $\ker(d\otimes1_R)$ in $V\otimes_F R$. For any $R$-algebra $S$ and $k\in K(S)$, evaluation $C\to S$ sends the equation $(d\otimes1_R)(w)=0$ to $kw_S=w_S$. Conversely, use $S=R\otimes_F C$ with its universal $K$-point $c\mapsto1\otimes c$; the equation $kw_S=w_S$ is exactly $(d\otimes1_R)(w)=0$, up to switching the two scalar factors. Hence $I\otimes_F R$ is precisely the vectors fixed by $K$ over every further $R$-algebra. Tensor evaluation and the factor switches are the linear maps determined on pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Proposition 4.31, printed p.96, fixed vectors after every algebra extension; expressed by the kernel of the restricted coaction minus the trivial coaction.

proof.text: The kernel $K$ is normal: for every $R$, $h\in H(R)$ and $k\in K(R)$, the homomorphism law [def-sc-group-scheme] gives $q(h^{-1}kh)=q(h)^{-1}1q(h)=1$. If $w\in I\otimes_F R$, then after every $R\to S$ and for $k\in K(S)$, $k(h_Sw_S)=h_S(h_S^{-1}kh_S)w_S=h_Sw_S$. Step 3 therefore shows that $h$ preserves $I\otimes_F R$. Take $R=F[H]$ and the universal point corresponding to the identity map of $F[H]$. Its action on $x\otimes1$ is the given coaction $\rho_H(x)$, so for $x\in I$ this coaction lies in $I\otimes_F F[H]$. The coaction identities restrict by the injective tensor inclusions of step 1. Thus $I$ is an $H$-subcomodule, and $v\in I$ by hypothesis. Minimality gives $W\subseteq I$. Its restricted $K$-coaction is consequently $w\mapsto w\otimes1$, which proves scheme-theoretic triviality on $W$.

source.place: Lemma 5.15 and its conjugation computation, printed p.102; universal-point formulation avoids any density or reducedness assumption.

proof.text: Write $A=F[G]$, $B=F[H]$ and $i=q^*:A\to B$. Apply [lem-pc-cech-exact] with module $A$: the augmentation is injective and its image is the equalizer of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ in $D=B\otimes_A B$. This algebra and its two structure maps are given by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. They define points $h_1,h_2\in H(D)$ with $q(h_1)=q(h_2)$. Therefore $h_1^{-1}h_2\in K(D)$, and step 4 gives $h_2w=h_1w$ for every $w\in W\otimes_F D$. Choose an $F$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $W$, and write $\rho_H(e_j)=\sum_l e_l\otimes b_{lj}$. Evaluating this equality at $h_1,h_2$ and comparing basis coefficients gives $b_{lj}\otimes1=1\otimes b_{lj}$. Exactness supplies a unique $a_{lj}\in A$ with $i(a_{lj})=b_{lj}$. Define $\rho_G(e_j)=\sum_l e_l\otimes a_{lj}$ and extend $F$-linearly. Then $(1_W\otimes i)\rho_G=\rho_H$.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101, factorization of a representation trivial on the kernel. Agent-written affine-coordinate argument using Stacks Tag 023M, descent-lemma-ff-exact, descent.tex, the augmented complex (equation-extended-complex); its full exactness is the cited lem-pc-cech-exact.

proof.text: Because $q$ is a group homomorphism, $i$ commutes with comultiplications and counits. Apply $1_W\otimes i\otimes i$ to the two proposed coassociativity maps for $\rho_G$. The factorization of step 5 turns their images into $(\rho_H\otimes1_B)\rho_H$ and $(1_W\otimes\Delta_B)\rho_H$, which agree. Step 1 and injectivity of $i$ from step 5 show $1_W\otimes i\otimes i$ is injective, so the two original maps agree. For the counit, $\epsilon_A=\epsilon_B i$ gives $(1_W\otimes\epsilon_A)\rho_G=(1_W\otimes\epsilon_B)\rho_H=1_W$. Thus $\rho_G$ is a rational $G$-coaction with exactly the required pullback. If $\rho'_G$ has the same pullback, injectivity of $1_W\otimes i$ gives $\rho'_G=\rho_G$. Together with steps 2 and 4 this proves every assertion; no finite-type, centrality or reducedness assumption was used.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101, homomorphism and uniqueness clauses; coaction laws and uniqueness checked explicitly through the injective coordinate map.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.31, printed p.96, Lemma 5.15, printed p.102, and Theorem 5.13, printed p.101; their normal-invariants/quotient route, with explicit split-linear-map and Amitsur-coordinate arguments extending the finite-type source to the stated arbitrary affine groups. Amitsur exactness: Stacks Tag 023M (descent-lemma-ff-exact), descent.tex.
